{{Navbar-Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker}}
'''Palomar Gas Transmission Pipeline''' is a cancelled natural gas pipeline in the United States.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oregonbusiness.com/2495-palomar-gas-partners-withdraw-application/|title=oregonbusiness.com|website=oregonbusiness.com|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs from GTN pipeline, central Oregon, Oregon to Columbia River northwest of Portland, with Molalla interconnect, Oregon.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tcenergy.com/announcements/2008/2008-12-11palomar-gas-transmission-files-application-for-a-certificate-to-build-pipeline-in-oregon/|title=tcenergy.com|website=tcenergy.com|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref>

*'''Owner: '''Palomar Gas Transmission LLC<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tcenergy.com/announcements/2008/2008-12-11palomar-gas-transmission-files-application-for-a-certificate-to-build-pipeline-in-oregon/|title=tcenergy.com|website=tcenergy.com|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref>
*'''Capacity: '''1.3 Bcf/d<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tcenergy.com/announcements/2008/2008-12-11palomar-gas-transmission-files-application-for-a-certificate-to-build-pipeline-in-oregon/|title=tcenergy.com|website=tcenergy.com|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref>

*'''Diameter: '''36 in<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tcenergy.com/announcements/2008/2008-12-11palomar-gas-transmission-files-application-for-a-certificate-to-build-pipeline-in-oregon/|title=tcenergy.com|website=tcenergy.com|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref>
